rows.label: Operating Profit (EBIT)
rows.source: Operating profit derived two ways that meet exactly: gross profit plus other income less operating expenses less the expected credit loss allowance, disposal, reclassification and foreign exchange lines; and profit before tax less finance income plus finance costs. FY2025 5,202,783 = 3,867,060 - 353,447 + 1,689,170. FY2024 5,863,029 = 2,266,780 - 234,214 + 3,830,463.
rows.derivedFormula: Operating Profit (EBIT) = Gross Profit - Operating Expenses

rows.label: Net Finance Costs
rows.formula: Net Finance Costs = finance costs minus finance income
rows.source: gap fill 2026-10-13 (run e): net finance costs = finance costs less finance income, the arithmetic this row already follows in the two earlier columns (FY2025 finance costs 1,689,170 less finance income 353,447 = 1,335,723 as stored; FY2024 3,830,463 less 234,214 = 3,596,249 as stored). For H1 2026 the file holds finance costs of 550,139 and no finance income in that column, so net finance costs = 550,139. Not a full reconciliation of the H1 2026 column: operating profit 1,780,809 less net finance costs 550,139 leaves 1,230,670 against a stored profit before tax of 2,165,226, a difference of 934,556 that the H1 2026 column does not itemise in this file.
